The macOS build runs this same termwiz parser (window/src/os/macos, all eight .rs files, carries no OSC handling of its own and names no semantic state), the mux protocol (mux/src/lib.rs, 1441 lines) has zero "semantic" and no unhandled-OSC verb, and the CLI at this tag reads no prompt state (wezterm/src/cli/get_text.rs:34,86-87 prints text or colour/style escapes only). macOS additionally offers no default-launch log surface for dropped OSCs.

tests.reason: Untestable (no way): WezTerm 20240203-110809-5046fc22 on macOS records each OSC 133 mark but exposes neither it nor a command-exit status, so it cannot observe 133 D or the complete A/C/D cycle. Read tag 20240203-110809-5046fc22 (5046fc225992db6ba2ef8812743fadfdfe4b184a): term/src/terminalstate/performer.rs:882-884 is FinalTermSemanticPrompt::CommandStatus { .. } => {} (an empty arm, no status stored), the other mark arms at :845-880 store only a pen semantic type, and term/src/terminalstate/mod.rs:2704 get_semantic_zones returns SemanticZone spans with no status field. No surface reads them back on default launch: mux/src/lib.rs has zero "semantic", the CLI's 19 verbs (CliSubCommand, wezterm/src/cli/mod.rs:77-166) read no zones, wezterm/src/cli/get_text.rs:34,86-87 prints text or escapes only, and the macOS frontend (window/src/os/macos, eight .rs files) names no semantic state. The upstream Linux row records the same empty arm at performer.rs:904-906 (e2a98e1b8af1); this arm is shared core term code, not a frontend path.
